recipes.title: Universal Frittata
steps: 1. Preheat broiler.
2. Sauté fillings in cast iron skillet until tender.
3. Whisk eggs, milk, salt. Pour over fillings.
4. Cook on stovetop quiet until edges set (5-7m).
5. Broil 3-5m until golden and puffed.

recipes.title: Master Overnight Oats
steps: 1. Combine equal parts oats and liquid in a jar.
2. Shake well.
3. Refrigerate overnight.
4. Eat cold or warm up next morning.

recipes.title: Homestead Pancakes
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients.
2. Mix wet ingredients.
3. Combine gently. Lumps are good.
4. Fry on hot greased griddle.

recipes.title: Liquid Gold Master Stock
steps: 1. Dump bones and scraps into large pot.
2. Cover with water.
3. Simmer 4-12 hours (stove) or 24h (slow cooker).
4. Strain and freeze.

recipes.title: Fridge Cleanout Soup
steps: 1. Sauté trinity in oil.
2. Add stock and tomatoes.
3. Add hard veg (potatoes), simmer 15m.
4. Add soft veg (corn/beans), simmer 5m.
5. Finish with vinegar and herbs.

recipes.title: Beef & Barley Stew
steps: 1. Coat beef in flour. Sear hard. Remove.
2. Sauté veg in beef fat.
3. Deglaze with wine.
4. Return beef. Add stock and barley.
5. Simmer covered low for 2 hours.

recipes.title: Creamy Potato Leek Soup
steps: 1. Sweat leeks in butter until soft.
2. Add potatoes and broth.
3. Simmer 20 mins until tender.
4. Blend until smooth. Season heavily.

recipes.title: Perfect Roast Chicken
steps: 1. Dry bird thoroughly.
2. Salt inside and out.
3. Place in cast iron skillet (on veg bed if using).
4. Roast at 425°F for 60-80 mins (165°F thigh).
5. Rest 15 mins before carving.

recipes.title: Pork Carnitas
steps: 1. Cut pork into chunks. Season.
2. Put in Dutch Oven with onion/orange/water.
3. Bake covered 300°F for 3 hours.
4. Uncover. Crank to 400°F to crisp fat (20m).

recipes.title: Ratio Meatloaf
steps: 1. Soak crumbs in milk.
2. Mix all ingredients gently.
3. Form loaf.
4. Bake 350°F for 60 mins.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie
steps: 1. Mix meat and veggies with gravy in baking dish.
2. Spread mashed potatoes on top. Seal edges.
3. Bale 400°F until gravy bubbles and potatoes brown.

recipes.title: No-Knead Artisan Bread
steps: 1. Mix shaggy dough. Cover. Wait 12-18 hours.
2. Preheat Dutch Oven to 450°F.
3. Drop dough into hot pot.
4. Bake covered 30 mins. Uncovered 15 mins.

recipes.title: Soft White Sandwich Loaf
steps: 1. Knead all ingredients 10 mins.
2. Rise 1 hr.
3. Shape and place in loaf pan. Rise 45m.
4. Bake 350°F for 30-35 mins.

recipes.title: Perfect Rice (Absorption)
steps: 1. Rinse rice well.
2. Boil water/rice. Cover tightly.
3. Low simmer 18 mins.
4. Remove from heat. Keep covered 10 mins (Crucial). Fluff.

recipes.title: Flaky Biscuits
steps: 1. Cut cold butter into flour/baking powder.
2. Stir in milk just until combined.
3. Pat out, fold over 3 times (creates layers).
4. Cut rounds. Bake 425°F for 12-15 mins.

recipes.title: 3:1 Vinaigrette
steps: 1. Whisk or shake in jar until creamy.

recipes.title: Béchamel (White Sauce)
steps: 1. Melt butter. Whisk in flour. Cook 1 min.
2. Slowly whisk in milk.
3. Simmer until thickened.

recipes.title: Pantry Marinara
steps: 1. Sauté aromatics.
2. Add tomatoes and herbs.
3. Simmer 20 mins.

recipes.title: Strawberry Jam (Canning)
steps: 1. Mix berries/pectin. Boil.
2. Add sugar. Hard boil 1 min.
3. Fill hot jars. 1/4 inch headspace.
4. Water bath process 10 mins.

recipes.title: Beef Jerky
steps: 1. Marinate meat 12-24 hours.
2. Dehydrate at 160°F for 4-6 hours.
3. Done when it cracks but doesn't snap.

recipes.title: Dried Apple Rings
steps: 1. Peel, core, slice.
2. Dip in lemon water to stop browning.
3. Dehydrate 135°F for 6-10 hours until leathery.

recipes.title: Sauerkraut
steps: 1. Shred cabbage.
2. Massage with salt until liquid releases.
3. Pack in jar under liquid weight.
4. Ferment 1-4 weeks.

recipes.title: Fermented Garlic Honey
steps: 1. Fill jar 3/4 with garlic.
2. Cover with honey.
3. Burp daily. Wait 1 month.

recipes.title: Lard Pie Crust
steps: 1. Cut lard into flour/salt.
2. Mix egg, vinegar, water. Pour into flour.
3. Mix until just combined. Don't overwork.
4. Chill 1 hour before rolling.

recipes.title: Skillet Cornbread
steps: 1. Melt drippings in cast iron skillet in 425°F oven.
2. Mix dry. Mix wet.
3. Combine.
4. Pour into hot skillet (listen for sizzle).
5. Bake 20 mins.

recipes.title: Chicken & Dumplings
steps: 1. Remove chicken from bone. Return meat to boiling broth.
2. Mix dough. Roll flat.
3. Cut into strips.
4. Drop into boiling broth.
5. Cover. Simmer 15 mins. Do not peek.

recipes.title: Bread & Butter Pickles
steps: 1. Salt veg and let stand 3 hours. Drain.
2. Boil brine (vinegar/sugar/spices).
3. Add veg. Heat to boil.
4. Pack hot jars. Water bath 10 mins.

recipes.title: Canned Applesauce
steps: 1. Cook apples in water until soft.
2. Mash or run through food mill.
3. Reheat to boil.
4. Pack hot jars.
5. Process 20 mins.

recipes.title: Zucchini Relish
steps: 1. Salt veg overnight. Drain and rinse.
2. Boil syrup of sugar/vinegar/spices.
3. Add veg. Simmer 30 mins.
4. Pack jars. Process 10 mins.

recipes.title: Survival Frittata
steps: 1. Preheat boiler (if available) or prepare skillet lid.
2. Whisk eggs and liquid distinctively.
3. Sauté mix-ins in an oven-safe skillet.
4. Pour egg mixture over mix-ins. Do not stir.
5. Cook on low heat until edges are set.
6. Transfer to oven/broiler to finish top, or cover with lid to steam.

recipes.title: Pantry Stir Fry
ingredients: Sauce: Soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ginger
steps: 1. Mix sauce ingredients in a small cup.
2. Heat oil in wok or skillet until smoking.
3. Sear protein quickly. Remove.
4. Stir fry vegetables until crisp-tender.
5. Return protein and add carbs.
6. Pour sauce over everything and toss to coat.

recipes.title: Depression Era Pasta
steps: 1. Boil pasta in salted water. Reserve 1 cup water before draining.
2. In the same pot, sauté aromatics or mix-ins.
3. Add tomato sauce and heat through.
4. Toss pasta with sauce, adding reserved water to thin if needed.

recipes.title: Stone Soup
steps: 1. Brown any meat or bones in the bottom of the pot.
2. Add liquid and bring to a simmer.
3. Add sturdy vegetables (potatoes/carrots). Simmer 20m.
4. Add soft vegetables and grains. Simmer 15m.
5. Season aggressively.

recipes.title: Savory Oatmeal Bowl
steps: 1. Boil oats in salted liquid.
2. While hot, stir in an egg (it will cook in the oats) or top with fried egg.
3. Add soy sauce, sesame oil, or whatever savory condiments you have.

recipes.title: Red Beans & Rice
steps: 1. Sauté onion and pepper (and meat if using).
2. Add beans and cover with water by 2 inches.
3. Simmer until beans are creamy (1.5 - 2 hours).
4. Mash some beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
5. Serve over white rice.

recipes.title: Tuna Casserole
steps: 1. Boil noodles al dente.
2. Mix drained tuna, soup, peas, and noodles.
3. Pout into baking dish.
4. Top with crushed crackers.
5. Bake at 350F for 20-25 mins until bubbly.

recipes.title: Basic Sourdough Loaf
steps: 1. Dissolve starter in water.
2. Mix in flour and salt until shaggy dough forms. Rest 30m.
3. Perform 4 sets of 'Stretch and Folds' every 30 mins.
4. Bulk Rise: Let sit at room temp for 4-8 hours until doubled.
5. Shape into a round. Place in banneton/bowl. Fridge overnight.
6. Bake in Dutch Oven: 450F (20m lid on, 25m lid off).

recipes.title: Survival Hardtack
steps: 1. Mix ingredients into a very stiff dough.
2. Roll out to 1/2 inch thickness.
3. Cut into 3x3 squares.
4. Poke holes using a nail/chopstick (prevents puffing).
5. Bake 375F for 30 mins. Flip. Bake 30 mins more.
6. Cool completely. Should be hard as a brick.

recipes.title: Campfire Bannock
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients.
2. Add oil and enough water to make a pliable dough.
3. Form into a patty (1 inch thick).
4. Fry in a greased skillet over coals, flip when golden.
5. PRO TIP: Can also wrap around a stick and roast.

recipes.title: Simple Yeast Bread
steps: 1. Bloom yeast in warm water with sugar for 5 mins.
2. Mix flour and salt. Add yeast water.
3. Knead 10 mins until smooth.
4. Rise 1 hour (doubled).
5. Punch down, shape loaf. Rise 30 mins.
6. Bake 400F for 30-35 mins.

recipes.title: Flour Tortillas
steps: 1. Cut fat into dry ingredients.
2. Add water, knead until smooth.
3. Divide into 8 balls. Rest 20 mins (Critical step!).
4. Roll paper thin.
5. Cook on HOT dry skillet, 30s per side (until bubbly).

recipes.title: Muscle Meat Jerky
steps: 1. Slice meat 1/4 inch thick. Remove ALL fat.
2. Marinate 12-24 hours.
3. Pat dry.
4. Dehydrate at 160F (or oven lowest setting door cracked) for 4-6 hours.
5. Done when it bends and cracks (white fibers visible) but doesn't snap.

recipes.title: Basic Sauerkraut
steps: 1. Shred cabbage finely.
2. Massage salt into cabbage until it releases liquid (brine).
3. Pack tightly into jar. Ensure cabbage is submerged in liquid.
4. Weigh down (bag of water or glass weight).
5. Ferment 3-4 weeks at room temp. Burp jar daily if needed.

recipes.title: Canned Tomatoes (Water Bath)
steps: 1. Score tomatoes, boil 1m, peel skins.
2. Pack into sterilized jars.
3. Add 1 tbsp lemon juice per pint (Critical for acid safety).
4. Leave 1/2 inch headspace.
5. Process in boiling water bath: 40 mins for pints, 45 for quarts.

recipes.title: Rabbit Stew
steps: 1. Dust rabbit pieces in flour, salt, pepper.
2. Brown in hot fat (bacon grease is best). Remove.
3. Sauté veggies.
4. Return rabbit, cover with cider/broth.
5. Simmer gently 1.5 - 2 hours until falling off bone.

recipes.title: Pan Fried Trout
steps: 1. Score skin of fish lightly.
2. Dredge in seasoned cornmeal.
3. Fry in hot butter/oil over medium heat.
4. 4-5 mins per side. Flesh flakes easily when done.

recipes.title: Venison Chili
steps: 1. Brown venison with onions.
2. Add spices and toast for 1 min.
3. Add remaining ingredients.
4. Simmer low and slow (venison is lean, don't boil hard).

recipes.title: Corned Beef Hash
steps: 1. Boil potato dice for 5 mins to soften. Drain.
2. Fry onion and potatoes in oil until starting to crisp.
3. Crumble in corned beef.
4. Press down with spatula to form crust. Flip and crisp other side.

recipes.title: Pantry Shakshuka
steps: 1. Sauté onion/garlic.
2. Add tomatoes and spices. Simmer 5 mins.
3. Make 4 divots in the sauce.
4. Crack eggs into divots.
5. Cover pan. Simmer 5-7 mins until whites set.

recipes.title: Lentil Tacos
steps: 1. Simmer lentils in water until soft (20m). Drain excess liquid.
2. Mash partially with fork.
3. Stir in taco seasoning.
4. Serve in tortillas.

recipes.title: Stovetop Rice Pudding
steps: 1. Combine rice, milk, sugar in pot.
2. Simmer medium-low, stirring often (scorches easily).
3. Cook until thickened (15-20m).
4. Add cinnamon/raisins off heat.

recipes.title: One Pot Chili Mac
steps: 1. Combine macaroni, chili, tomatoes, and 1 tomato-can of water in pot.
2. Bring to boil.
3. Simmer covered, stirring occasionally, until pasta is tender (10-12m).
4. Top with cheese if you have it.

recipes.title: Spam Musubi Bowl
steps: 1. Cut Spam into slices.
2. Fry until crispy.
3. Add splash of soy sauce and sprinkle of sugar to pan to glaze.
4. Serve glazed Spam over rice with crumbled nori.

recipes.title: Canned Fruit Cobbler
ingredients: 1 box Yellow Cake Mix (or flour/sugar/butter mix)
steps: 1. Pour fruit into baking dish.
2. Sprinkle dry cake mix over fruit.
3. Slice butter thinly and arrange over top.
4. Bake 375F for 35-40 mins until golden and bubbly.

recipes.title: Salmon Patties
steps: 1. Drain salmon.
2. Mix all ingredients. If too wet, add more crumbs.
3. Form into patties.
4. Pan fry in oil until golden brown on both sides.

recipes.title: Cowboy Caviar
steps: 1. Rinse all canned beans well.
2. Mix in bowl.
3. Toss with Italian dressing or vinegar/oil mix.
4. Serve as dip with chips or side salad.

recipes.title: Traditional Pemmican
steps: 1. Pound dried meat into a fluff/powder.
2. Melt tallow.
3. Mix meat powder and tallow 1:1 by weight.
4. Press into molds/blocks.
5. Will last years without refrigeration.

recipes.title: Refrigerator Pickles
steps: 1. Slice veggies into jars.
2. Boil vinegar, water, and salt to dissolve.
3. Pour hot brine over veggies.
4. Cool. Fridge. Ready in 24 hours.

recipes.title: Basic Lye Soap (Hot Process)
steps: 1. OUTDOORS: Add Lye to Water. (NEVER WATER TO LYE). Mix.
2. Melt fat. Coll lye and fat to ~100F.
3. Add Lye Water to Fat.
4. Stick lend to 'Trace' (pudding consistency).
5. Pour into mold. Insulate. Cut after 24 hours. Cure 4 weeks.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Noodles
steps: 1. Boil noodles.
2. Whisk peanut butter, soy, sugar, and splash of hot water.
3. Drain noodles.
4. Toss hot noodles with sauce. Top with crushed peanuts/onions.

recipes.title: Loaded Baked Potato
steps: 1. Poke holes in potato. Bake 400F for 1 hour (or microwave 10m).
2. Slice open.
3. Top efficiently with heated chili and cheese.

recipes.title: Leftover Fried Rice
steps: 1. Heat oil in skillet until smoking.
2. Fry veggies.
3. Add rice (break up clumps). Fry until hot.
4. Push aside, scramble egg in empty spot.
5. Mix everything with soy sauce.

recipes.title: Three Bean Salad
steps: 1. Drain and rinse kidney beans. Drain others.
2. Mix beans.
3. Mix 1/2 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup oil, 1/4 cup sugar.
4. Toss beans with dressing. Marinade overnight for best taste.

recipes.title: Dandelion Green Salad
steps: 1. Harvest young greens before they flower (less bitter).
2. Wash thoroughly in cold water.
3. Toss with wild onion and dressing.

recipes.title: White Pine Needle Tea
ingredients: Handful White Pine Needles (flexible needles in clusters of 5)
steps: 1. Roughly chop needles to release oils.
2. Bring water to a boil, then remove from heat.
3. Steep needles for 5-10 mins (do not boil needles, it destroys Vitamin C).
4. Strain and drink.

recipes.title: Leached Roasted Acorns
steps: 1. Shell acorns and crush into large chunks.
2. Leach tannins by soaking in repeated changes of water until no longer bitter (takes 1-3 days).
3. Drain and pat dry.
4. Roast at 350F for 45 mins until fragrant and crunchy.
5. Grind into flour or eat as nuts.

recipes.title: Rocket Stove Corncakes
steps: 1. Mix cornmeal and salt. Pour boiling water over until a thick paste forms.
2. Let sit 5 mins.
3. Heat cast iron on rocket stove.
4. Fry thin patties in fat until crispy on both sides.

recipes.title: Haybox (Insulated) Rice
steps: 1. Bring rice and water to a rolling boil for 2 mins.
2. Immediately place tight lid on pot.
3. Place pot inside a haybox (box filled with straw/wool/blankets).
4. Seal box and wait 1 hour. Rice will cook using its own thermal mass.
5. Saves 15 mins of fuel.

recipes.title: Dry Cured Salt Pork
steps: 1. Rub pork thoroughly with salt/sugar mix.
2. Pack in a wooden box or crock with layers of salt between meat.
3. Store in cool, dark place (root cellar).
4. Over 2 weeks, moisture will be drawn out.
5. Keeps for 6-12 months. Soak in water to desalt before cooking.

recipes.title: Grandma's Fire Cider
steps: 1. Chop all aromatics and pack into a jar.
2. Cover with ACV.
3. Shake daily for 4 weeks.
4. Strain and mix with honey to taste.
5. Take a tablespoon daily for immunity.

recipes.title: Stinging Nettle Soup
steps: 1. Wear gloves to harvest and wash nettles.
2. Sauté onion and potatoes until soft.
3. Add broth and simmer 15 mins.
4. Add nettles. Cook 2-3 mins (cooking removes the sting).
5. Blend until smooth. Add cream if available.

recipes.title: Classic Pemmican
steps: 1. Pound dried meat into a coarse powder.
2. Mix meat and berries.
3. Pour hot melted tallow over mixture (1:1 ratio by weight).
4. Form into small bars. Let cool and harden.
5. Ultimate survival food; stores for years.

recipes.title: Sautéed Cattail Shoots
steps: 1. Harvest shoots from clean water source. Peel away outer green layers to find the white core.
2. Wash thoroughly.
3. Sauté in butter for 3-5 mins.
4. Taste is similar to cucumber or asparagus.
recipes.processing_note: Ensure cattails are harvested from clean, non-polluted water. See Guide 12.1 for ID and 12.4 for cleaning.

recipes.title: Roasted Chicory Coffee
steps: 1. Scrub roots clean. Dice finely.
2. Roast in oven (or by campfire) at low heat (250F) for 3-4 hours until dark brown and brittle.
3. Grind into a powder.
4. Brew like coffee. Naturally caffeine-free but bitter and robust.
recipes.processing_note: Scrub roots thoroughly. See Guide 12.4 for roasting and grinding details.

recipes.title: Ash-Roasted Potatoes
steps: 1. Poke holes in potatoes.
2. Wait for a fire to burn down to deep white hot ashes.
3. Dig a hole in the ash, bury potatoes, cover with 2 inches of ash.
4. Bake for 30-45 mins until soft when poked with a stick.
5. Brush off ash and eat with salt.

recipes.title: Elderberry Flu Syrup
steps: 1. Simmer berries and spices in water for 45 mins until liquid is reduced by half.
2. Strain out berries.
3. Let liquid cool to lukewarm (below 110F).
4. Stir in raw honey to keep enzymes alive.
5. Standard survival medicine for colds and flu.
recipes.processing_note: WARNING: MUST COOK berries to destroy cyanide precursors. Never eat raw. See Guide 12.4.

recipes.title: Anti-Inflammatory Golden Milk
steps: 1. Whisk all ingredients in a small pot.
2. Heat until steaming but not boiling.
3. Drink before bed for joint health and recovery.

recipes.title: Leached Acorn Pancakes
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients.
2. Whisk in wet ingredients.
3. Fry on a hot griddle. Acorn flour adds a nutty, earthy flavor.
recipes.processing_note: Acorns MUST be leached to remove bitter/toxic tannins. See Guide 12.4 for leaching steps.

recipes.title: Wild Garlic Compound Butter
steps: 1. Mash wild garlic into butter.
2. Roll into a log using parchment paper.
3. Freeze or refrigerate. Use for flavoring meat and bread.

recipes.title: Sautéed Lamb's Quarters
steps: 1. Wash leaves thoroughly; remove tough stems.
2. Sauté garlic in oil.
3. Add greens and wilt for 2-3 mins. Nutrient-dense wild spinach substitute.

recipes.title: Rocket Stove Quick Stew
steps: 1. Bring broth to boil on rocket stove.
2. Add veggies and meat.
3. Simmer until veggies rehydrate.
4. Stir in potato flakes until desired thickness reached.

recipes.title: Solar Oven Sun-Bread
steps: 1. Place dough in a dark-colored pot with a lid.
2. Set solar oven in direct sun, adjusting every 30 mins.
3. Bake until internal temp reaches 190F (takes 2-4 hours depending on sun).
4. Very low fuel cost but requires clear skies.

recipes.title: Canned Spiced Beets
steps: 1. Boil beets until skins slip off.
2. Slice or leave whole (if small).
3. Pack into jars. Cover with hot brine (vinegar/sugar/spices).
4. Water bath process 30 mins.

recipes.title: Potted Beef (Confit)
steps: 1. Slow roast beef until falling apart.
2. Shred beef finely. Mix with juices and some melted fat.
3. Pack tightly into jars. Cover top with 1 inch of pure melted fat.
4. Once fat hardens, it seals out air. Store in cold root cellar.

recipes.title: Burdock Root & Beef Stew
steps: 1. Sauté meat and onion.
2. Add burdock root. Burdock is very fibrous; needs long simmering.
3. Cover with broth. Simmer 1 hour until root is tender. Nutty, artichoke-like flavor.
recipes.processing_note: Peel thick skin before cooking. See Guide 12.4 for digging and prep.

recipes.title: Primitive Cattail Flour
steps: 1. Dig roots from clean mud. Scrub clean.
2. Peel bark to reveal starchy core.
3. Mash cores in a bucket of water. Starch will settle at bottom.
4. Pour off water. Dry the white sludge into flour.
5. Use 1:1 with wheat flour for survival bread.
recipes.processing_note: Harvest from clean water. Refer to Guide 12.4 for the starch settling method.

recipes.title: Rose Hip Jam (Vitamin C)
steps: 1. REMOVE ALL SEEDS from hips (they have irritating hairs).
2. Simmer hips in water until soft.
3. Mash and add sugar.
4. Boil until thick. Extremely high in Vitamin C.
recipes.processing_note: MANDATORY: Remove all seeds and irritating hairs. See Guide 12.4 for removal technique.

recipes.title: Ash-Roasted Corn in Husk
steps: 1. Soak whole ears in water for 10 mins (prevents burning).
2. Place directly on hot coals. Cover with ash.
3. Rotate every 5 mins.
4. Peel back charred husks; corn will be perfectly steamed.

recipes.title: Hot Stone Broth
steps: 1. Heat clean stones (NOT sandstone/wet rocks) in fire until glowing.
2. Place water and ingredients in a wooden bowl or skin bag.
3. Drop hot stones into water one by one Using tongs/sticks.
4. Water will boil instantly. Replace stones as they cool until food is cooked.

recipes.title: Pickled Garlic Cloves
steps: 1. Pack garlic into small jars.
2. Boil vinegar/salt brine.
3. Pour over garlic. Water bath process 5 mins or keep in fridge.
4. Mellows the garlic; prevents botulism in oil storage.

recipes.title: Salt-Cured Egg Yolks
steps: 1. Bury yolks in salt/sugar mix in a container.
2. Refrigerate (or root cellar) for 4 days.
3. Remove and rinse. Dry in low oven or dehydrator until firm like parmigiano cheese.
4. Grating over pasta/rice adds intense savory flavor.

recipes.title: Elderflower Fritters
steps: 1. Whisk flour, egg, and liquid into a thin batter.
2. Dip flower clusters into batter, holding the stem.
3. Fry in hot oil until golden (about 1 min).
4. Snip off the stems and serve with honey.

recipes.title: Purslane & Egg Stir-fry
steps: 1. Wash purslane; use stems and leaves.
2. Sauté garlic.
3. Add purslane and stir-fry for 1 min.
4. Add beaten eggs and scramble until set. High in Omega-3 fatty acids.

recipes.title: Roasted Groundnuts (Apios)
steps: 1. Harvest tubers from wet areas. Scrub well.
2. Boil for 10 mins (helps soften the skin).
3. Toss with oil and salt.
4. Roast at 400F for 20 mins until crunchy outside and potato-like inside.

recipes.title: Spit-Roasted Rabbit
steps: 1. Rub rabbit with salt and wild garlic.
2. Skewer on a green (unseasoned) hardwood branch.
3. Suspend over hot coals (not flames).
4. Rotate slowly for 45-60 mins until juices run clear. Baste with fat if available.

recipes.title: Skillet Soda Bread
steps: 1. Mix dry. Add liquid until it forms a shaggy dough.
2. Form into a flat disc.
3. Place in a preheated cast iron skillet with a lid.
4. Bake over medium heat (or in coals) for 12 mins per side.

recipes.title: Canned Pickled Pike/Bass
steps: 1. Soak fish in salt brine for 24 hours. Rinse.
2. Pack into jars with onion slices.
3. Cover with boiling vinegar/sugar/spice brine.
4. Water bath process 15 mins. Wait 1 week for flavors to develop and bones to soften.

recipes.title: Survival Mushroom Powder
steps: 1. Slice mushrooms paper thin.
2. Dehydrate at 125F until brittle.
3. Grind in a mortar and pestle into a fine powder.
4. Store in airtight jars. Adds incredible umami/protein to any soup or stew.

recipes.title: Traditional Birch Syrup
steps: 1. Tap birch trees in late spring. Sap is lower sugar than maple (100:1 ratio).
2. Boil sap in a large flat pan over high fire.
3. As it thickens, lower heat significantly. Birch syrup burns easier than maple.
4. Bottle when it reaches 66% sugar content. Dark, spicy, and mineral-rich.
recipes.processing_note: Birch sap spoils quickly. Process immediately. See Guide 12.4 for tapping safety.

recipes.title: Survival 'Joe's' Mead (Quick)
steps: 1. Shake honey and warm water in a jug until dissolved.
2. Add orange, raisins, and yeast.
3. CAP LOOSELY or use a balloon with a pinhole (to let CO2 escape).
4. Ferment in dark place for 2 months.
5. Syphon off the clear liquid. Potent and easy.

recipes.title: Wild Sumac 'Lemonade'
steps: 1. Rub sumac clusters in cold water to release tart malic acid. Do not use hot water (it releases bitter tannins).
2. Strain through cheesecloth to remove fine hairs.
3. Sweeten to taste. High in Vitamin C and very refreshing.
recipes.processing_note: Use ONLY cold water to avoid bitter tannins. See Guide 12.4 for ID vs Poison Sumac.

recipes.title: Viking Pine Bark Bread
steps: 1. Harvest the white, soft inner bark from a fallen or thinned pine tree. Do not girdle live trees.
2. Dry the bark and grind into a fine flour.
3. Mix 1 part bark flour to 2 parts wheat flour.
4. Add water/salt to form dough. Bake as flatbreads. Rescued many through winter famines.
recipes.processing_note: Ethical harvesting is critical. Harvest Cambium layer only. See Guide 12.4 for prep.

recipes.title: Cast Iron Campfire Pizza
steps: 1. Heat oil in a heavy cast iron skillet over coals.
2. Lay dough in skillet. Fry for 3-5 mins until bottom is brown.
3. Flip dough. Quickly add toppings.
4. Cover skillet with a lid or foil. Place hot coals on top of lid to melt cheese from above.

recipes.title: Clay-Baked River Fish
steps: 1. Stuff fish with onions. Leave scales on.
2. Coat the entire fish in a 1-inch layer of wet clay.
3. Place the clay 'brick' directly into hot coals.
4. Bake for 30 mins. Crack open the clay; the scales and skin will peel off with the clay, leaving perfectly steamed flesh.

recipes.title: Simple Dried Apple Rings
steps: 1. Slice apples into thin rings. Dip in lemon water.
2. String onto a line or layout on racks.
3. Dry near a woodstove or in the sun until leathery and no moisture remains.
4. Keeps for months in jars.

recipes.title: Honey & Onion Cough Syrup
steps: 1. Slice onion thinly. Layer in a jar with honey.
2. Let sit overnight at room temp. The honey will draw out the onion juice.
3. Strain. Take a spoonful for coughs and sore throats. Very effective antibacterial properties.

recipes.title: Willow Bark Tea (Natural Aspirin)
ingredients: 1 tsp Dried White Willow Bark (inner bark)
steps: 1. Harvest inner bark from willow twigs. Dry and crush.
2. Simmer 1 tsp bark in water for 10-15 mins.
3. Contains salicin, the precursor to aspirin. Drink for pain relief and fever reduction.

recipes.title: Chickweed & Walnut Pesto
steps: 1. Wash chickweed thoroughly. It is a mild, corn-like flavored green.
2. Blend or crush nuts and garlic.
3. Add chickweed and oil. Blend until smooth.
4. Use over pasta or as a bread spread. High in vitamins.

recipes.title: Daylily Bud Fritters
steps: 1. Harvest buds when firm and green/orange but not open.
2. Dip in batter.
3. Fry in shallow oil until golden.
4. Taste is similar to green beans or okra.

recipes.title: Sweet Ash-Roasted Onions
steps: 1. Place whole onions directly into hot ashes/coals.
2. Roast for 20 mins until the outer skins are black and charred.
3. Pull from fire. Peel away the burnt layers.
4. The inner heart will be sweet, steamed, and perfectly cooked.

recipes.title: Solar Oven Brownies
steps: 1. Mix batter and pour into a thin dark metal pan.
2. Place in solar oven. Align with sun.
3. Bake 1.5 - 3 hours depending on solar intensity.
4. Passive cooking that keeps the 'kitchen' cool in summer.

recipes.title: Pickled Garlic Scapes
steps: 1. Chop scapes into 2-inch lengths.
2. Pack into jars.
3. Pour hot pickling brine over scapes.
4. Water bath process 10 mins. Crunchy, mild garlic flavor.

recipes.title: Traditional Survival Mincemeat
steps: 1. Combine all ingredients in a large pot.
2. Simmer for 1 hour to integrate flavors.
3. Pack into jars. The high sugar/acid/fat content preserves the meat for winter.
4. Traditionally used for pies but can be eaten as a high-calorie energy food.

recipes.title: Quick Dandelion Wine
steps: 1. Steep petals in hot water for 2 days.
2. Strain. Add sugar and yeast.
3. Ferment in a jug with an airlock.
4. Bottle after 2 months. Best after 6-12 months. Sunny and floral.

recipes.title: Charcoal Tummy Biscuits
steps: 1. Mix ingredients into a stiff dough.
2. Roll thin and cut into crackers.
3. Bake until dry and hard.
4. Eat 1-2 when experiencing stomach upset or bloating. Home-made charcoal must be made from clean hardwood.

recipes.title: Wild Garlic Mustard Pesto
steps: 1. Garlic mustard is an invasive species; harvest as much as you want.
2. Blanch leaves for 30s to reduce bitterness (optional).
3. Pulse all ingredients in a blender.
4. Sharp, garlicky, and peppery. Great for foraged pizza.

recipes.title: Cattail Pollen Gold Cakes
steps: 1. Shake yellow pollen from cattail heads in early summer.
2. Sift out any bugs/fluff.
3. Mix with flour and standard pancake wet ingredients.
4. The pollen adds a beautiful gold color and a sweet, floral nutty taste.

recipes.title: Hot Stone Tea
steps: 1. Heat clean stones in fire.
2. Place water and herbs in a wooden or wax-coated container.
3. Add hot stones until steaming. Effectively brews tea without needing a metal pot.

recipes.title: Dutch Oven Coal-Bread
steps: 1. Pre-heat Dutch oven in coals.
2. Dust bottom with cornmeal. Add dough.
3. Place lid on. Cover lid with 2 inches of hot coals.
4. Place 3-4 small coals underneath the oven.
5. Bake for 30-45 mins. The 'coals-on-top' method mimics a kitchen oven perfectly.

recipes.title: Old World Salted Herring
steps: 1. Clean fish but leave bones in (they soften).
2. Layer fish and salt 1:1 in a wooden barrel or ceramic crock.
3. Press down with a weight.
4. Brine will form. Leave for 2 weeks. Keeps for 1 year in cool storage. Soak in water for 24h before eating.

recipes.title: Pressure Canned Chicken
steps: 1. Pack raw chicken tightly into clean jars. Leave 1 inch headspace.
2. Add 1/2 tsp salt per pint. Do not add liquid (it makes its own broth).
3. Process at 11 lbs pressure (adjust for altitude): 75 mins for pints, 90 mins for quarts.
4. Safe, shelf-stable meat for years.

recipes.title: Fire & Onion Tonic
steps: 1. Grate onion into honey.
2. Add a heavy pinch of cayenne.
3. Take by the spoonful for severe congestion and sore throats.

recipes.title: Staghorn Sumac Spice (Za'atar style)
steps: 1. Harvest red sumac heads in late summer.
2. Dry thoroughly in a solar dehydrator.
3. Pound in a mortar and pestle to remove the fuzzy red coating from the hard seeds.
4. Sift to keep only the red powder.
5. Tangy, lemony spice that keeps for years. Great on meat or in hummus.

recipes.title: Eastern White Cedar Tea
steps: 1. Steep a small amount of cedar leaves in hot water (do not boil).
2. Very high in Vitamin C. Use sparingly; do not drink daily as it can be hard on kidneys in large amounts.
3. Survival classic for preventing scurvy in winter.

recipes.title: Flatbread on a Hot Rock
steps: 1. Find a large, flat, clean stone (granite is best; avoid river rocks).
2. Heat the stone in the fire until it sizzles when touched with water.
3. Scrape off ash. Lay thin dough discs directly on the rock.
4. Flip when the edges curl. Perfectly charred primitive bread.

recipes.title: Solar Oven Berry Muffins
steps: 1. Pour batter into a dark muffin tin.
2. Place in solar oven for 1.5 - 2 hours.
3. Muffins stay incredibly moist due to the low-temp steam environment of the solar cooker.

recipes.title: Salt-Cured Quail Eggs
steps: 1. Bury raw eggs (in shell) in a container of salt.
2. Wait 3-4 days. The salt draws moisture through the shell, curing the egg inside.
3. To eat, boil briefly or bake. The texture is firm and the flavor intensified. Keeps for weeks without refrigeration.

recipes.title: Pickled Wild Mushrooms
steps: 1. Pre-boil mushrooms to ensure safety and remove excess moisture.
2. Pack into jars with aromatics.
3. Cover with boiling vinegar/oil/salt mixture.
4. Water bath process 10 mins. Gourmet survival staple.

recipes.title: Fermented Honey Garlic
steps: 1. Fill a jar with garlic cloves. Cover with raw honey.
2. Flip jar daily. It will bubble as it ferments.
3. After 2 weeks, garlic is soft and honey is thin/infused.
4. Nature's strongest antibiotic. Eat a clove at the first sign of illness.

recipes.title: Spit-Roasted Partridge
steps: 1. Season the bird inside and out with salt, pepper, and herbs.
2. Truss the bird or skewer it onto a spit.
3. Roast over medium coals, turning frequently.
4. Baste with butter or oil until skin is crisp and meat is just cooked through (approx 15-20 mins).

recipes.title: Crispy Partridge Fingers
steps: 1. Slice partridge breasts into uniform strips.
2. Dip strips into beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in seasoned flour or breadcrumbs.
3. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
4. Fry strips for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.

recipes.title: Braised Partridge with Cabbage
steps: 1. Brown the partridges in a dutch oven with fat or bacon.
2. Remove birds, add onion and carrots, and sauté until soft.
3. Add cabbage and stir to coat.
4. Return birds to the pot, add stock, and cover.
5. Simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until meat is tender.

recipes.title: Homestead Rabbit Stew
steps: 1. Brown rabbit pieces in a heavy pot.
2. Add onions and carrots, sauté for 5 mins.
3. Add liquid and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer.
4. Add potatoes after 1 hour.
5. Simmer till meat falls off the bone (usually 2 hours).

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Wild Rabbit
steps: 1. Season flour with salt, pepper, and paprika.
2. Dip rabbit pieces in milk, then dredge through the seasoned flour.
3. Heat lard in a large skillet until hot.
4. Fry rabbit pieces on medium heat, turning to ensure even browning (approx 20-30 mins total).

recipes.title: Rabbit Confit
ingredients: Lard or Duck Fat (enough to cover)
steps: 1. Salt the rabbit pieces and let sit for 1 hour. Rinse and pat dry.
2. Place meat in a deep baking dish with herbs and garlic.
3. Melt fat and pour over meat until completely submerged.
4. Cook at 225°F for 3-4 hours until meat is incredibly tender.
5. Store in the fat to preserve, or sear in a pan to serve.

recipes.title: Classic Brunswick Stew
steps: 1. Simmer squirrels in water until meat is tender enough to de-bone.
2. Remove meat, discard bones, and return meat to broth.
3. Add all vegetables and simmer on low for another 2 hours.
4. Season with salt, pepper, and a dash of hot sauce if desired.

recipes.title: Smoked & Braised Squirrel
steps: 1. Smoke squirrels at 225°F for 1.5 hours to infuse flavor.
2. Transfer to a pot with onion, cider, and honey.
3. Cover and braise on low for another 2 hours until tender.
4. Shred the meat for tacos or sliders.

recipes.title: Roasted Dandelion Coffee
steps: 1. Scrub roots clean and chop into small uniform pieces.
2. Roast in a skillet or oven at 350°F until dark brown and aromatic.
3. Grind the roasted roots into a coarse powder.
4. Brew like regular coffee (1 tbsp per cup of water).

recipes.title: Master Acorn Flour
steps: 1. Shell the acorns and grind the nutmeats into a coarse meal.
2. Place in a cloth bag and submerge in running water or change water multiple times until bitterness (tannins) is gone.
3. Spread the leached meal on a tray and dry thoroughly in a low oven or sun.
4. Grind into a fine flour and use 1:1 with wheat flour in recipes.

recipes.title: White Pine Needle Tea
steps: 1. Strip needles from branches. Avoid the brown ones.
2. Chop needles into small pieces to release oils.
3. Steep in hot (not boiling) water for 5-10 minutes.
4. Strain and drink for a massive dose of Vitamin C.

recipes.title: Wild Rose Hip Jelly
steps: 1. Simmer rose hips in water until soft. Mash and strain through a fine jelly bag.
2. Measure 3 cups of the rose hip juice into a pot.
3. Add pectin and lemon juice, bring to a hard boil.
4. Add sugar and boil for 1 minute. Skim foam.
5. Process in a water bath for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Wild Cattail 'Asparagus'
steps: 1. Pull young cattails from the marsh. Peel back the outer layers to reach the white core.
2. Slice into 4-inch pieces.
3. Sauté in butter with salt and pepper for 5-7 minutes until tender.
4. Tastes like a cross between cucumber and asparagus.

recipes.title: Wild Burdock Root Stew
steps: 1. Sauté meat and onions in a pot.
2. Add burdock root, carrots, and enough water to cover.
3. Simmer for 45-60 minutes until roots are tender like parsnips.
4. Season with soy sauce for an earthy, deep flavor.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Venison Leg
steps: 1. Make small slits in the meat and insert garlic slivers.
2. Rub with salt, pepper, and chopped herbs.
3. Sear in a hot pan, then transfer to a roasting dish with stock and wine.
4. Roast at 300°F until internal temp reaches 135°F for medium-rare.
5. Rest for at least 20 minutes before carving.

recipes.title: Traditional Moose Jerky
ingredients: 2 lbs Moose Lean Meat (sliced thin across grain)
steps: 1. Mix marinade ingredients and coat meat slices thoroughly.
2. Refrigerate for 12-24 hours.
3. Arrange slices on dehydrator racks or a low oven (160°F).
4. Dry for 6-10 hours until meat is leathery but still bendable.
5. Store in airtight jars for long-term survival protein.

recipes.title: Wild Duck with Orange & Honey
steps: 1. Prick the duck skin to help fat render.
2. Mix orange juice, honey, soy, and zest into a glaze.
3. Roast ducks at 350°F, brushing with glaze every 15 minutes.
4. Remove when skin is dark mahogany and crisp.
5. Let rest. Meat should be slightly pink.

recipes.title: Pheasant Normande
ingredients: 1 cup Heavy Cream or Apple Cider
steps: 1. Brown pheasant pieces in butter and remove.
2. Sauté apples in the same pan until golden.
3. Return pheasant, add cider/cream, and cover.
4. Simmer until meat is tender (approx 45 mins).
5. Serve with the creamy apple sauce.

recipes.title: Fermented Garlic Honey
steps: 1. Fill a clean jar about 2/3 full with peeled garlic cloves.
2. Pour honey over the garlic until completely covered.
3. Close the lid and flip the jar to coat everything.
4. Loosen the lid daily to release built-up gases (burping).
5. Flip daily for 2 weeks. The honey will become runny and the garlic will darken.

recipes.title: Pine Pitch Drawing Salve
steps: 1. Melt the oil/lard in a double boiler (or a tin can in hot water).
2. Add the resin and stir until dissolved. Use a stick you can throw away.
3. Strain through a fine mesh or cheesecloth to remove bark/bugs.
4. Add beeswax for a firmer texture and charcoal to aid 'drawing' action.
5. Pour into a small tin. Apply to splinters, boils, or minor infections.

recipes.title: Survival Master Tonic (Fire Cider)
steps: 1. Place all solid ingredients into a quart jar.
2. Fill with apple cider vinegar until completely covered.
3. Use parchment paper under the lid to prevent corrosion.
4. Shake daily for 4 weeks.
5. Strain through cheesecloth and keep the liquid. Take a shot daily for immunity.

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Steel-Cut Porridge
steps: 1. Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
2. Stir in oats and reduce heat to a low simmer.
3. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. Stir in milk for creaminess if desired.
5. Top with butter and syrup.

recipes.title: Homestead Leftover Hash
ingredients: 1 cup Cooked Meat (Venison, Ham, or Beef)
steps: 1. Heat fat in a large cast-iron skillet.
2. Add onions and sauté until translucent.
3. Add potatoes and meat. Press down with a spatula to create a crust.
4. Fry until browned and crispy, flipping in sections.
5. Serve alongside or topped with fried eggs.

recipes.title: Fuel-Up Biscuits & Sausage Gravy
steps: 1. Brown sausage in a large skillet; do not drain fat.
2. Sprinkle flour over meat and stir for 1-2 minutes to cook raw flour taste.
3. Gradually whisk in milk, starting with 3 cups.
4. Simmer until thickened, adding more milk if too thick.
5. Season heavily with black pepper. Pour over split biscuits.

recipes.title: Field-Hand Cornmeal Mush
steps: 1. Mix cornmeal and cold water in a bowl to prevent lumps.
2. Slowly pour mixture into salted boiling water, stirring constantly.
3. Cook and stir until thick (about 5-10m).
4. Reduce heat, cover, and steam for 10-15m.
5. Serve hot with milk and sugar, or let set, slice, and fry in butter.

recipes.title: Overnight Sourdough Waffles
steps: 1. Night before: Mix starter, water, and flour. Cover and leave at room temp.
2. Morning: Beat eggs, butter, salt, and 1 tsp baking soda (optional for lift).
3. Fold egg mixture into the bubbly overnight sponge.
4. Cook in a hot waffle iron until steam stops rising.
5. Serve with fruit and honey.

recipes.title: Wild Berry Dutch Baby
steps: 1. Preheat oven and a 10-inch cast iron skillet to 425°F.
2. Whisk eggs, milk, flour, and sugar until smooth.
3. Melt 2 tbsp butter in the hot skillet, then pour in batter.
4. Scatter berries over the top.
5. Bake for 15-20 minutes until puffed and golden brown. Do not open oven!

recipes.title: Wild Leek & Potato Soup
steps: 1. Sauté leeks in butter until soft.
2. Add potatoes and stock; bring to a boil.
3. Simmer until potatoes are tender (20m).
4. Mash roughly for texture or blend for smoothness.
5. Stir in cream and season. Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Old Man's Venison Chili
steps: 1. Brown venison and onion in a large pot.
2. Add spices and stir for 1 minute.
3. Mix in tomatoes and beans (drained).
4. Simmer on low for at least 1-2 hours to mellow flavors.
5. Serve with cornbread and shredded cheese.

recipes.title: Roasted Harvest Squash Soup
steps: 1. Roast squash halves at 400°F until soft (45m). Scoop out flesh.
2. Sauté onion and apples in a pot.
3. Add squash flesh and stock. Simmer for 10m.
4. Blend until smooth.
5. Stir in spices and a touch of maple syrup if desired.

recipes.title: Rabbit & Barley Forest Stew
steps: 1. Dredge rabbit pieces in flour and brown in a heavy pot.
2. Remove rabbit; sauté veggies for 5m.
3. Return rabbit to pot with stock, barley, and herbs.
4. Simmer gently for 1.5 hours until meat falls off the bone.
5. Season well. The barley will thicken the broth into a rich stew.

recipes.title: Fisherman's Survival Chowder
ingredients: 2 lbs White Fish (Bass, Trout, or Cod)
steps: 1. Fry bacon/salt pork in pot until crisp. Remove bits.
2. Sauté onion in the fat.
3. Add potatoes and just enough stock/water to cover. Simmer 10m.
4. Add fish chunks and milk. Simmer gently (do not boil!) until fish flakes.
5. Stir in corn and reserved bacon bits. Season with plenty of pepper.

recipes.title: Pan-Seared River Trout
steps: 1. Pat fish dry. Season with salt and pepper.
2. Dredge in a light coating of cornmeal.
3. Melt butter in a hot skillet.
4. Sear fish for 3-4 minutes per side until skin is crispy.
5. Garnish with lemon and parsley.

recipes.title: Homestead Stuffed Peppers
steps: 1. Cut tops off peppers and remove seeds.
2. Sauté meat and onion until browned.
3. Mix meat with rice and 1 cup of tomato sauce.
4. Stuff peppers and place in a baking dish.
5. Pour remaining sauce over top. Bake at 375°F for 45m.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie (Homestead Style)
steps: 1. Brown meat and onion in a large skillet.
2. Add veggies and gravy; simmer for 5m.
3. Transfer to a baking dish.
4. Spread mashed potatoes over the top and fluff with a fork.
5. Bake at 400°F until top is golden and bubbly.

recipes.title: Grandpa's Fried Squirrel
steps: 1. Season squirrel pieces heavily.
2. Dredge in flour mixed with paprika.
3. Heat lard in a cast iron skillet until shimmering.
4. Fry pieces until golden brown and cooked through (about 10m per side).
5. Serve with biscuits and gravy.

recipes.title: Braised Rabbit with Cider
steps: 1. Brown rabbit pieces in butter; remove.
2. Sauté onions until soft.
3. Return rabbit and add cider and rosemary.
4. Simmer covered for 1 hour until tender.
5. Remove rabbit, stir in cream, and reduce sauce until thickened.

recipes.title: No-Knead Dutch Oven Bread
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients, then stir in water until a shaggy dough forms.
2. Cover and let rise at room temp for 12-18 hours.
3. Preheat oven and Dutch oven to 450°F.
4. Pour dough onto parchment and place in hot pot.
5. Bake covered for 30m, then uncovered for 15m until crusty.

recipes.title: Old-Time Johnnycakes
steps: 1. Mix cornmeal and salt in a bowl.
2. Pour boiling water over and stir until a stiff paste forms.
3. Let sit for 5 minutes.
4. Form into small patties and fry in butter until brown on both sides.
5. Serve with honey or maple syrup.

recipes.title: Survival Hardtack (Pilot Bread)
steps: 1. Mix flour and salt. Add water gradually until a stiff dough forms.
2. Roll out to 1/2 inch thickness.
3. Cut into squares and poke holes in both sides with a fork.
4. Bake at 375°F for 30m per side until dry and 'hard as a rock'.
5. Proper storage will allow these to last years. Soak in coffee/soup before eating.

recipes.title: Skillet Bannock (Trail Bread)
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients. Add liquid to form a dough.
2. Shape into a flat disc.
3. Fry in a greased skillet on low heat for 8-10m per side.
4. It should sound hollow when tapped.
5. Perfect for trail cooking or emergencies.

recipes.title: Traditional Salt-Rising Bread
steps: 1. Mix cornmeal, sugar, and boiling water. Keep in warm place (12-18h) until bubbly and funky-smelling.
2. Mix in milk and 1 cup flour to make a sponge. Let rise again (2-4h).
3. Add remaining flour to make a bread dough.
4. Shape into a loaf, let rise one final time (1h).
5. Bake at 375°F until golden. This bread is leavened by bacteria, not yeast!

recipes.title: Grandma's Pickled Beets
steps: 1. Boil beets until tender. Slip off skins and slice.
2. Combine vinegar, sugar, and spices in a pot; bring to a boil.
3. Add beets and simmer for 5m.
4. Pack into hot jars, leaving 1/2 inch headspace.
5. Process in a boiling water bath for 30m.

recipes.title: Hot Pepper Jelly
steps: 1. Pulse peppers in a processor until finely minced.
2. Combine peppers, vinegar, and sugar in a large pot. Bring to a rolling boil.
3. Stir in pectin. Boil hard for 1 minute.
4. Skim foam and pour into hot sterile jars.
5. Process in water bath for 5m. Best served over cream cheese.

recipes.title: Small-Batch Mason Jar Sauerkraut
steps: 1. Toss cabbage and salt in a large bowl. Massage for 10m until water is released.
2. Pack cabbage into a clean quart mason jar, pressing down hard to keep submerged in its own brine.
3. Use a weighted glass or a smaller jar to keep cabbage under the liquid.
4. Cover with a cloth or loose lid. Store in cool, dark place.
5. Sample after 2 weeks; continue for 4 weeks for deep tang.

recipes.title: Dried Fruit Leathers
ingredients: 4 cups Fruit Puree (Berries, Apples, or Peaches)
steps: 1. Puree fruit until completely smooth. Stir in honey and lemon.
2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3. Spread puree evenly (about 1/8 inch thick).
4. Dry in oven at lowest setting (140-170°F) or dehydrator for 6-8 hours.
5. Peel off and roll up. Should be pliable, not brittle.

recipes.title: Pressure-Canned Venison
steps: 1. Raw pack: Fill hot jars with raw meat cubes, leaving 1 inch headspace.
2. Add 1/2 tsp salt per pint (1 tsp per quart). Do not add liquid; meat will make its own juice.
3. Wipe rims, apply lids.
4. Process in pressure canner at 11 lbs (altitude dependent).
5. Pints: 75m, Quarts: 90m. The results are incredibly tender.

recipes.title: Spruce Tip Syrup
ingredients: 2 cups Bright Green Spruce Tips (Spring only)
steps: 1. Boil water and sugar to make a simple syrup.
2. Add clean spruce tips. Remove from heat immediately.
3. Let steep for at least 2 hours (or overnight for stronger flavor).
4. Strain and bottle.
5. High in Vitamin C. Excellent on pancakes or in tea.

recipes.title: Sautéed Spring Dandelion Greens
ingredients: 1 tbsp Olive Oil or Bacon Fat
steps: 1. Wash greens thoroughly in cold water.
2. Sauté garlic and red pepper in fat until fragrant.
3. Add greens and toss until wilted (just like spinach).
4. Squeeze a bit of lemon over the top to cut any bitterness.
5. Serve as a nutrient-dense side dish.

recipes.title: Wild Burdock Root Chips
steps: 1. Slice burdock root as thinly as possible into rounds (a mandolin helps).
2. Soak in cold water for 5m to remove 'earthy' bite, then pat completely dry.
3. Fry in 350°F oil until edges slightly curl and turn brown.
4. Drain on paper towels.
5. Salt immediately. They have a unique, nutty, artichoke-like flavor.

recipes.title: Sumac 'Lemonade' (Staghorn)
steps: 1. Place sumac heads in a jar of cold water.
2. Mash slightly with a spoon to break surfaces.
3. Let steep in cold water for 2-4 hours. Do not use boiling water as it releases bitter tannins.
4. Strain through a fine cloth (coffee filter) to remove tiny hairs.
5. Sweeten with honey. Tastes remarkably like pink lemonade.

recipes.title: White Pine Needle Tea
ingredients: 1 handful Eastern White Pine Needles (bright green)
steps: 1. Finely chop or bruise the pine needles to release oils.
2. Bring water to a boil, then remove from heat.
3. Add needles and steep for 5-10 minutes. Do not boil needles directly as it destroys Vitamin C.
4. Strain into a cup.
5. Enjoy the citrusy, resinous flavor. Extremely high in Vitamin C and A.

recipes.title: No-Bake Nut Cookies
ingredients: 3 1/2 c. bite size shredded rice biscuits
steps: In a heavy 2-quart saucepan, mix brown sugar, nuts, evaporated milk and butter or margarine.
Stir over medium heat until mixture bubbles all over top.
Boil and stir 5 minutes more. Take off heat.
Stir in vanilla and cereal; mix well.
Using 2 teaspoons, drop and shape into 30 clusters on wax paper.
Let stand until firm, about 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Cheeseburger Potato Soup
ingredients: 1 lb. of extra lean ground beef
1 1/2 c (6 oz.) shredded Cheddar cheese, divided
12 sliced bacon, cooked, crumbled and divided
steps: Wash potatoes; prick several times with a fork.
Microwave them with a wet paper towel covering the potatoes on high for 6-8 minutes.
The potatoes should be soft, ready to eat.
Let them cool enough to handle.
Cut in half lengthwise; scoop out pulp and reserve.
Discard shells.
Brown ground beef until done.
Drain any grease from the meat.
Set aside when done.
Meat will be added later.
Melt butter in a large kettle over low heat; add flour, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Gradually add milk; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and bubbly.
Stir in potato, ground beef, salt, pepper, 1 cup of cheese, 2 tablespoons of green onion and 1/2 cup of bacon.
Cook until heated (do not boil).
Stir in sour cream if desired; cook until heated (do not boil).
Sprinkle with remaining cheese, bacon and green onions.

recipes.title: Rhubarb Coffee Cake
steps: Cream sugar and butter.
Add egg and beat well.
To creamed butter, sugar and egg, add alternately buttermilk with mixture of flour, salt and soda.
Mix well.
Add rhubarb and vanilla.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan and add Topping.

recipes.title: Nolan'S Pepper Steak
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb. round steak (1-inch thick), cut into strips
1 can drained tomatoes, cut up (save liquid)
steps: Roll steak strips in flour.
Brown in skillet.
Salt and pepper.
Combine tomato liquid, water, onions and browned steak. Cover and simmer for one and a quarter hours.
Uncover and stir in Worcestershire sauce.
Add tomatoes, green peppers and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve over hot cooked rice.

recipes.title: Quick Barbecue Wings
ingredients: chicken wings (as many as you need for dinner)
steps: Clean wings.
Flour and fry until done.
Place fried chicken wings in microwave bowl.
Stir in barbecue sauce.
Microwave on High (stir once) for 4 minutes.

recipes.title: Broccoli Salad
ingredients: 5 green onions, sliced or 1/4 c. chopped red onion
steps: Trim off large leaves of broccoli and remove the tough ends of lower stalks. Wash the broccoli thoroughly. Cut the florets and stems into bite-size pieces. Place in a large bowl. Add bacon, onions and raisins. Combine remaining ingredients, stirring well. Add dressing to broccoli mixture and toss gently. Cover and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours. Makes about 6 servings.

recipes.title: Eggless Milkless Applesauce Cake
ingredients: 1 tsp. each: cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg
steps: Mix Crisco with applesauce, nuts and raisins.
Sift dry ingredients and add.
Mix well.
Put in a greased and floured loaf pan or tube pan.
Bake in loaf pan at 350° to 375° for 45 to 60 minutes, layer pan at 375° for 20 minutes or tube pan at 325° for 1 hour.

recipes.title: Grandma Hanrath'S Banana Breadfort Collins, Colorado
steps: Cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs, salt and soda, then bananas and flour.
Add nuts.
Mix well.
Bake in loaf pan at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.title: Prize-Winning Meat Loaf
steps: Mix well.
Press firmly into an 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Bake in preheated moderate oven.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Let stand 5 minutes before slicing.
Makes 8 servings.

recipes.title: Smothered Round Steak(Servings: 4)
steps: Alex Patout says, "Smothering is a multipurpose Cajun technique that works wonders with everything from game to snap beans.
It's similar to what the rest of the world knows as braising.
The ingredients are briefly browned or sauteed, then cooked with a little liquid over a low heat for a long time."

recipes.title: Corral Barbecued Beef Steak Strips
ingredients: 2 lb. round steak 1/2 to 3/4-inch thick, sliced in strips 1/8-inch thick (or thinner) and 3 1/2 to 4-inches long (easily sliced if partially frozen)
steps: Brown strips in cooking oil.
Pour off drippings.
Combine tomato sauce, water, brown sugar, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Add sauce and onion to meat slices.
Cover and cook slowly, stirring occasionally 30 minutes or until meat is tender. Serve over rice or buttered noodles.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.

recipes.title: One Hour Rolls
steps: Put flour into a large mixing bowl.
Combine sugar, milk, salt and oil in a saucepan and heat to boiling; remove from heat and let cool to lukewarm.
Add yeast and mix well.
Pour into flour and stir.
Batter will be sticky.
Roll out batter on a floured board and cut with biscuit cutter.
Lightly brush tops with melted oleo and fold over.
Place rolls on a cookie sheet, put in a warm place and let rise for 1 hour.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes. Yield: 2 1/2 dozen.

recipes.title: Quick Coffee Cake(6 Servings)
steps: Mix 3 tablespoons fat with granulated sugar.
Add egg and beat until creamy.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt thoroughly.
Add to sugar mixture alternately with milk.
Add vanilla. Spread batter evenly in a greased 8-inch square baking pan.
Mix brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over batter.
Dot with 2 tablespoons fat.
Bake at 350° (moderate oven) for 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Angel Biscuits
steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt together.
Cut in margarine, dissolve yeast in warm water.
Stir into buttermilk and add to dry mixture.
Cover and chill.

recipes.title: Chocolate Mint Bars
steps: Mix together and bake in 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Top should spring back when touched lightly; do not overbake.
Cool completely, then spread with mint layer.

recipes.title: Beer Bread
steps: Stir the ingredients together and put in a greased and floured loaf pan.
Bake at 425 degrees for 50 minutes.
Drizzle melted butter on top.

recipes.title: Chicken Divan
ingredients: 1/4 c. chopped onion (or as much as you want)
steps: Melt margarine in skillet; saute onions and celery.
Remove from heat.
Stir in flour and curry powder.
Drain mushrooms and keep juice.
Add water to juice to make 1/2 cup liquid.
Stir liquid and soup into flour mixture; add mushrooms.
Cook until thick.
Arrange broccoli and cubed chicken in a large baking dish. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 20 minutes or in microwave until cheese is melted.

recipes.title: Mexican Cookie Rings
steps: Sift flour, baking powder and salt together.
Cream together butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks and vanilla.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Mix in sifted dry ingredients.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Push wooden spoon handle through center (twist).
Shape into rings.
Dip each cookie into candies.
Place on lightly greased baking sheets.
Bake in 375° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool on racks.
Serves 2 dozen.

recipes.title: Chicken Casserole
steps: Mix all ingredients together in baking dish.
Cover and bake at 350° for 2 1/2 hours.
Bake the last 45 minutes, uncovered, to brown top of chicken.

recipes.title: Moist Devil'S Food Cake
steps: Sift together the flour, soda and salt; set aside.
Combine shortening and sugar in a bowl.
Beat until creamy.
Add egg yolks; beat well.
Combine cocoa, water and vanilla to make 1 cup; mix well.
Add to batter.
Add flour mixture alternately with milk.
Beat well after each addition; set aside.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form when beater is lifted.
Fold into batter. Bake in two 9-inch greased cake pans at 375° for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Dot'S Civil War Cake
steps: Combine and cook first 6 ingredients.
Bring to boil and boil 5 minutes; cool.
Add sifted, dry ingredients to apple mixture. Stir and blend only.
Add nuts.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 16.

recipes.title: Potato Casserole
steps: Peel and dice potatoes; place in bowl of cold, salted water. Drain potatoes and dry on paper towels.
Mix 1/2 cup butter, onions, soup, sour cream and cheese; stir well.
Add potatoes to mixture and pour into a 2 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Crush cornflakes, mix with remaining butter.
Sprinkle cornflakes and butter on top of potato mixture.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.

recipes.title: Apple Crisp
steps: Mix 1/2 cup of sugar and cinnamon.
Spread on apples.
Mix 1/4 cup sugar, flour, salt, cornflake crumbs and oleo.
Spread mixture on apples.

recipes.title: Consomme Chicken
steps: Add enough liquid to chicken soup and consomme to make 4 cups of water.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.title: Brown Rice
steps: Put in a covered 1 1/2-quart dish.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.

recipes.title: Funnel Cake
ingredients: 2/3 c. milk (more if batter is too thick)
steps: Sift first 5 ingredients together in a bowl.
Mix egg and milk together; add to dry ingredients.
Beat until smooth.
Hold finger over bottom of a funnel; pour in some batter.
Remove finger to let batter drop.
Drop batter in a spiral motion into pan filled with 1 inch of hot oil (375°).
Fry until golden brown, turning once.
Remove from pan; drain on a paper towel.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve hot.

recipes.title: Pound Cake
ingredients: 3 c. plain flour (cake flour may be substituted for plain flour)
1 to 2 Tbsp. flavoring (lemon, vanilla or almond or a combination of the 3)
steps: Have all ingredients at room temperature. Hand stir all dry ingredients together. Add eggs and stir. Add butter and Crisco and stir. Add milk and stir. Put batter in

mixer and beat at high speed until well blended. Add 1 to 2 teaspoons of your favorite flavoring and mix well. Pour batter into greased and floured tube pan. Place in cold oven. Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 to 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Beef And Spanish Rice Casserole
steps: Spray a 1-quart casserole dish with Pam.
Layer rice and meat, diced onion and grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Sweet-N-Sour Chicken
steps: Saute onion in 2 tablespoons shortening.
Add carrots, water and bouillon cubes.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Combine next 6 ingredients.
Add to vegetable mixture and cook until clear.
Add pepper, pineapple and chicken.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until heated through.
Serve with rice or angel hair noodles. Serves 6 people.

recipes.title: Pancakes
steps: Mix dry ingredients.
Add egg, margarine and buttermilk. Stir by hand until well blended.
Pour onto non-stick pan or griddle with a little oil added.
Cook until bubbly and turn over.

recipes.title: Red Cabbage And Apples
steps: In a saucepan filled with lightly salted boiling water, cook red cabbage for 5 minutes; then drain.

recipes.title: German Potato Salad
steps: Peel and cut potatoes in thin slices.
Fry bacon until crisp. Remove bacon from grease and reserve 1/2 cup drippings to make dressing.
Blend sugar, flour, salt and pepper.
Stir into bacon drippings to make smooth paste.
Add vinegar and water.
Boil 2 to 3 minutes.
Combine sauce, potatoes and onions in skillet.
Turn skillet off.
Cover with a towel (not a lid) and let stand at room temperature 3 or 4 hours.
Sprinkle with bacon.

recipes.title: Cutout Cookie
steps: Mix all ingredients.
Chill for several hours.
Cut out with cookie cutters.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Frost if you want to. Makes approximately 4 dozen.

recipes.title: Crisp Oatmeal Cookies
steps: Mix oats, brown sugar and oil; let stand overnight or 8 hours. Preheat oven to 325°.
Mix rest of ingredients into oat mixture. Drop by teaspoon onto greased baking sheet.
Bake 15 minutes. Cool completely before removing from baking sheet.

recipes.title: Good Sweet Muffins
steps: Heat oven to 400°.
Beat egg with fork.
Add remaining ingredients except blueberries and stir until flour is moistened. Batter should be lumpy.
Add blueberries, if desired.
Fill muffin cups 2/3 full.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Vanilla Creme Dessert
steps: Mix flour and melted margarine.
Pat mixture in 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Let cool.

recipes.title: St. Joseph'S Zeppole
steps: Combine water, butter, sugar and salt in saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add flour all at once, then beat with a wooden spoon for 1 minute or until mixture leaves sides of pan and forms a ball. Cool mixture.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each egg, until mixture has satin-like sheen.
Use pastry bag with large star tip and fill with mixture.
Make doughnut shape with pastry bag on greased cookie sheet.
Bake in 400° oven for 20 minutes or until puffed and well browned.
Cool.
Slice each zeppole in half and fill with the following filling.

recipes.title: Chicken Casserole
ingredients: 1 can cream of chicken or chicken mushroom soup
bite size pieces of 4 to 6 chicken thighs or any other chicken parts you wish to use
steps: Mix all together; pour into a 7 x 12-inch casserole.
Sprinkle with pepper and paprika.
Bake approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.

recipes.title: Apple Pie
steps: Put in unbaked pie shell.
Top apples with 2 tablespoons margarine with crust.
Brush milk on top of crust and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake on bottom shelf at 400° for 45 minutes.

recipes.title: 7-Up Cake
ingredients: 3 sticks real butter (preferably Land O Lakes)
steps: Mix sugar and butter thoroughly, then add egg, flour, egg, flour, etc. until all eggs and flour are mixed thoroughly, either with hand mixer or electric beater/mixer.
Then add lemon flavor and your 7-Up (the 7-Up will make the cake rise); add yellow food coloring which is optional.
Bake at 325° to 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour, depending on oven.
Insert toothpick after 45 minutes. Cook in Bundt pan. Let cool 25 minutes.
Cake is done.

recipes.title: Chocolate Pie
steps: Mix dry ingredients; add milk.
Beat in egg yolks.
Pour on 1 cup boiling water.
Mix and cook until thick.
Cool.
Pour in baked pie shell.
Cover with meringue and brown in oven.

recipes.title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Cake
steps: In saucepan, melt oleo; add cocoa.
Combine remaining ingredients and add oleo-cocoa mixture.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan for 30 minutes at 350°.
While still hot, punch holes in cake. Spread on cake, 1/2 cup peanut butter mixed with 1 1/2 tsp. oil.

recipes.title: Tamale Casserole
steps: Preheat oven to 350°.
Peel wrappers off tamales and chop in large bowl.
Drain hominy, olives and peppers.
Add them to tamales.
Mix well.
Place in 9 x 13 x 3-inch baking dish.
Spread out evenly.
Sprinkle cheese over top and olives if desired.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 8.
Serve with Spanish rice and corn chips.

recipes.title: Bonnie'S Bread
ingredients: 1 cake yeast or 3 pkg. dry yeast
steps: Can use dehydrated potato flakes.
Add flour as desired. Dough should be soft and elastic.
Bake as rolls or bread at 350°. Bread is done when it sounds hollow when tapped.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie
steps: Combine the first five ingredients and place in a 9 x 12-inch casserole dish.
Mix next four ingredients and pour over top of chicken mixture.
Do not stir.
Bake at 425° for 45 minutes to one hour until crust rises and browns.

recipes.title: Smoked Turkey Risotto
ingredients: 3 c. chicken stock or vegetable stock
3 green onions, including tops, sliced (1/3 c.)
1 c. arborio, basmati, or long-grain, white rice
4 oz. spinach, rinsed, trimmed and thinly sliced (2 c.)
steps: In medium-size saucepan, bring the stock to a boil over medium heat.
Lower the heat, add the artichoke hearts, cover and simmer for about 10 minutes or until tender.
With a slotted spoon, transfer the artichoke hearts to a bowl and cover to keep warm.

recipes.title: Watergate Cake
ingredients: 1 pkg. of pistachio instant pudding mix
steps: Combine box cake mix, oil, instant pudding, ginger ale, eggs, and pecans.
Pour into a 13 x 9-inch pan that has been greased and floured.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Cool and add topping when ready to serve. For topping the cake, mix cool whip, milk and pistachio instant pudding mix. Pour over cake and let set.

recipes.title: Plum Muffins
steps: Mix all ingredients together.
Drop into greased muffin tins. Bake at 325° for 15 to 20 minutes or until done.

recipes.title: Butternut Pound Cake
steps: Cream sugar and Crisco well.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Beat well.
Add flour and milk alternately on medium.
Last, add flavors.
Beat 2 minutes.
Heat oven to 325°.
Pour batter into greased and floured cake pan.
Bake for 1 hour.

recipes.title: Morning Glory Muffins
steps: Combine first 5 ingredients in a large mixing bowl; stir in carrots and next 4 ingredients.
Make a well in center of mixture. Combine vegetable oil and remaining ingredients.
Add to flour mixture, stirring until moistened.
Place paper baking cups in muffin pans.
Spoon batter into paper cups, filling 2/3 full. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove from pans immediately.
Makes 22 muffins.

recipes.title: Chicken Breasts With Wild Rice
ingredients: 1 3/4 c. quick cooking long grain and wild rice or plain rice
1 (10 3/4 oz.) can condensed cream of mushroom or chicken soup (undiluted)
1/4 c. cornflake crumbs or cracker crumbs
steps: Combine first 5 ingredients together.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch microwave dish.
Lay chicken breasts on top of rice mixture, with heavy side of breasts at corners of the dish.
Brush with melted butter or margarine and sprinkle evenly with cornflake crumbs.

recipes.title: Creole Green Beans
steps: Saute green pepper and onion in hot bacon drippings until tender. Add flour, salt, sugar and paprika.
Stir until blended. Add tomatoes and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Stir in green peas; heat through and serve.

recipes.title: Banana Bread
ingredients: 1 stick butter, cut in small pieces
steps: Mix eggs, bananas, butter and sugar in blender or food processor.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Add the two mixtures together.
Pour in greased pan and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

recipes.title: Sky High Biscuits
steps: Combine dry ingredients.
Cut in butter as you would for pie crust.
Add milk and egg quickly and stir briefly.
Knead for a few minutes.
Roll to 1-inch thickness.
Cut into biscuits.
Bake at 450° for 12 to 15 minutes on greased cookie sheets.

recipes.title: German Potato Salad
steps: Boil the potatoes until done.
Peel and slice while still warm.
Stir while pouring on the vinegar and hot grease.
Garnish with the bacon and chopped parsley, if available.
Sprinkle with sugar if too tart due to the vinegar.

recipes.title: Coconut Pie
steps: Mix flour, sugar and coconut in a bowl.
Beat eggs and add milk, butter and flavoring. Then add dry ingredients.
Pour into well greased pie plate and bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until golden brown.
This pie makes its own crust.

recipes.title: Bullets
steps: Mix together ground beef with salt and pepper and enough flour to hold meat together.
Roll into meat balls. Roll meat balls in more flour to coat. Drop meat balls into boiling water and cook. It will make its own gravy.
Serve over rice or mashed potatoes. May add more seasoning to taste as these are very bland.

recipes.title: Mom'S Pancakes
steps: Sift flour with baking powder, salt and sugar into a medium bowl.
With rotary beater, beat egg.
Add milk and butter; beat until well mixed.
Pour this into dry ingredients; beat only until combined.
Batter will be lumpy.

recipes.title: Fruit Bars
ingredients: 1 c. cut up dates or whole raisins
steps: Heat oven to 350°.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, almond extract and eggs.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Spread dough in greased pan (13 x 9 x 2-inch).
Bake until light brown, 30 to 35 minutes.

recipes.title: Chinese Hamburger
steps: Brown hamburger. Add onion and celery until transparent; drain. Add soups, water, rice, soy sauce and pepper. Transfer to a casserole dish. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Top with chow mein noodles and cook for 10 minutes more.

recipes.title: Hungarian-Stuffed Peppers
steps: Prepare peppers (remove white sections).
Mix ground beef, rice, egg and seasoning.
Fill peppers; place in deep cooking vessel.
Cover with V-8.
Cook for 1 hour at 350°.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cup Cookies
ingredients: 1 (10 oz.) bag miniature Reese's peanut butter cups
steps: Cream butter, peanut butter, brown sugar and white sugar.
Beat in egg and vanilla.
Sift flour, baking soda and salt.
Add flour mixture to creamed mixture.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Spray miniature muffin pans with nonstick spray and place balls of dough in pans.
Do not spread dough in cups.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes or lightly browned.
Remove from heat and immediately press peanut butter cup into each cookie until only top shows.
Let cool in tins for 10 to 15 minutes.
These freeze well.
Makes about 4 dozen.

recipes.title: Egg Cheese Souffle
steps: In greased baking dish, place croutons and Velveeta.
Mix eggs, milk, mustard, salt, onion powder and pepper.
Pour on top of cheese.
Place crumbled bacon on top.
Bake at 325° for 50 minutes.

recipes.title: Apple Bread
steps: Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in egg.
Stir together flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, raisins and pecans.
Add to sugar mixture alternately with applesauce.
Pour into greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Bake in 325° oven for 1 hour or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

recipes.title: Homemade Noodles
steps: Stir together.
Roll out as thin as you can on floured surface (use lots of flour).
Roll up and slice whatever width you want. Gently toss to unroll.
Drop in your favorite boiling broth. Gently boil about 8 minutes.
These can be frozen by spreading noodles out on floured cookie sheet.
Put in freezer until firm. Then store in freezer bags.

recipes.title: Chocolate Fudge
steps: Combine margarine, milk and sugar in Dutch oven.
Place over medium
heat
until
sugar	is dissolved.
Heat slowly to boiling. Cover and boil 5 minutes.	Turn off heat if electric stove.
If gas
stove,
turn
warmer
as low as possible.
Add marshmallows. Stir
until
dissolved.
Add each of chocolate, one at a
time. Stir
until
melted.
Add
vanilla	and nuts. Pour into 15 x 10 x 1-inch pan.
Cut when firm.
Makes about 5 pounds.

recipes.title: Fruit Cake
steps: Beat eggs; stir in sugar.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt. Combine with chocolate chips, nuts and cherries.
Fold in egg-sugar mixture.
Pour into well-greased and floured loaf pans. Place pan of water on bottom rack of oven and loaf pans on top rack.
Bake at 325° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.title: Brownie Pie
steps: Place flour, cocoa and sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Stir to mix well.
Add eggs, margarine, salt and vanilla.
Beat with a whisk for about 4 minutes.
Stir in nuts.
Pour into a greased 8-inch pie pan and bake in preheated 325° oven until done, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Pie will puff up and then settle down.
Serve slightly warm with ice cream or whipped cream.
Makes 8 servings.

recipes.title: Cream Puff Dessert
steps: Boil water and margarine.
Then add flour.
Let cook; then add eggs one at a time.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan, sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes until brown.
Cool.
Mix instant pudding, milk and softened cream cheese.
Spread on crust and top with Cool Whip.
Drizzle with chocolate syrup.
Chill 6 hours prior to serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Giblet Gravy
steps: Mix first 4 ingredients in saucepan and bring to boil.
Reduce to low-medium heat and add flour-water mixture.
Let simmer 5 to 10 minutes over low heat.

recipes.title: Nana'S Cornbread(For 9-Inch Iron Skillet Or 8 X 8-Inch Pan)
steps: Stir 1/2 teaspoon baking soda into 1 cup buttermilk.
Melt 1/4 cup bacon fat into pan you are using in the oven you are preheating.
Mix ingredients.
Bake at 425° for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Spoon Rolls
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Mix with other ingredients.
To bake, spoon batter into well-greased muffin tin about 2/3 full. Bake at 425° for 20 minutes or until golden brown. Will keep in refrigerator for 2 weeks if sealed in Tupperware bowl.

recipes.title: Chicago Crunchy Chocolate Chip Cookies
steps: Sift flour, baking soda and salt onto wax paper.
Preheat oven to moderate (350°).
Beat butter, margarine, brown sugar, granulated sugar, egg, milk and vanilla in a bowl until well blended.

recipes.title: Carrot Bread
steps: Mix all ingredients in order.
Bake in greased loaf pan for 1 hour at 350°.

recipes.title: Do-Unkles Pumpkin Cake
steps: Combine all ingredients together.
Mix at medium speed for 3 minutes.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Frost with cream cheese frosting or your favorite.

recipes.title: Colonial Cheese Biscuits
steps: These pancakes are as big as a dinner plate and formerly even bigger (12-inches in diameter!).
Nowadays you may find such big pancakes on the menu of a restaurant, but at home, we make them the dinner plate size.
They are either eaten as a savory (with smoked sausage or bacon) or as a sweet (plain with molasses or golden syrup or with apples).
Pancakes are best when made with yeast and they should be served piping hot.
Use two skillets when available. Keep the pancakes hot on steam, or covered in the oven.
Cold pancakes are awful!
The following recipe is a luxury one, for special occasions, as many eggs are used in preparing (instead of yeast).

recipes.title: Any Flavor Pan Dessert
steps: Mix the first 4 ingredients and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake 8 to 10 minutes at 350°.
Combine 1 cup whipped topping with cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Spread on top of baked layer and chill.
Mix pudding with milk and spread over second layer.
Chill 15 minutes before spreading the remaining whipped topping over the pudding.
Serves 16.

recipes.title: Apple Sour Cream Coffee Cake
ingredients: 1 1/4 c. apples, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Combine flour, soda and salt. In another bowl, cream butter and 1 cup sugar until fluffy. Add eggs and vanilla; mix well. Blend in flour mix, alternating with sour cream. In another bowl, mix together apples, cinnamon, 1/2 cup sugar and nuts. Spread half the batter in a greased 9-inch tube or Bundt pan. Sprinkle half the cinnamon-apple mix over the batter. Spoon in the rest of the batter and sprinkle on the rest of the cinnamon-apple mix. Bake at 375° for 40 to 50 minutes. Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodles
steps: Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat with an electric mixer, the sugar, margarine, shortening and eggs in a large mixing bowl.
Put flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt into flour sifter and add to the sugar mixture.
Stir until flour disappears.
Shape dough by rounding teaspoonfuls into balls.
Mix 2 teaspoons sugar and 2 teaspoons cinnamon; roll each ball in cinnamon sugar mixture. Place about 2 inches apart on cookie sheet.
Bake until set, about 8 to 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Spanish Meat Balls
steps: Mix well the first 9 ingredients; shape into small balls.
Put into a large greased casserole.
Heat soup, water and remaining chili powder; pour over meat balls.
Bake, covered, at 375° for 2 hours.
Yields 6 servings.

recipes.title: Fried Onion Rings
steps: Cut onions into 1/2-inch slices; separate rings. Place in a bowl; cover with ice water and let soak for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Mayonnaise Rolls
ingredients: 1 c. White Lily Self Rising Flour
steps: Mix well, fill muffin pans 1/3 full.
Bake at 400° until brown.
Makes about 6 rolls.

recipes.title: Etta'S Hungarian Coffee Cake
ingredients: 1/2 c. sour milk (add 1 Tbsp. vinegar or lemon juice to sour 1 c. milk)
steps: Mix sugar and shortening.
Add flour and salt until it crumbles.
Put aside 1/2 cup of this mixture for topping.
Add egg to remainder.
Add soda and baking powder to sour milk, then mix everything together.
Sprinkle crumbs on top.
(Optional: Sprinkle cinnamon and ground nuts on top.)
Bake for 35 minutes in a 9-inch cake pan or pie plate.

recipes.title: Gooey Butter Cake
ingredients: 1 box yellow or chocolate cake mix
steps: Preheat oven at 350°.
Mix cake mix with 1 egg and butter, melted.
Press into a 9 x 12 cake pan that has been greased and floured.
Then mix 2 eggs, cream cheese, 1 box powdered sugar and vanilla together.
Use a blender until all mixed, then pour over cake in pan and bake about 35 to 40 minutes at 350° or until you can stick a toothpick in and it comes out clean.
Cool, then cut into squares and eat.

recipes.title: Corn Pudding
steps: Mix flour, sugar, salt and pepper.
Add to corn.
Add melted butter. Add eggs.
Add milk.
Pour into greased casserole.
Place in a pan of water. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Serves 6.

recipes.title: Honey Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs and honey together.
Add sugar and mix again.
Mix coffee with baking powder and add margarine to the egg mixture.
Add baking soda, flour and cinnamon and beat together well.
Pour into greased cake pan.
Bake for 55 minutes to 1 hour.

recipes.title: Zucchini In Tomato Juice(From Weight Watchers)
steps: Cut zucchini in half lengthwise, then cut into cubes.
Put all ingredients in a saucepan and cook until the zucchini is tender.

recipes.title: Pineapple Casserole
steps: Mix sugar, flour and cheese.
Add pineapple; pour in greased 10 x 10-inch casserole.
Sprinkle crackers on top.
Pour melted butter over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Brunswick Stew
steps: Bring chicken to boil in salted water.
Reduce heat and simmer 1 hour, until tender.
Remove from both.
Add vegetables to broth and simmer until tender.
Strip chicken from bones in large pieces and add to stew last 5 minutes of cooking.

recipes.title: Cheese Ball
steps: Mix together cream cheese, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Finely chop onions, beef, olives and bell pepper. Add to cheese mixture and mix well. Chill at least 6 hours.
Shape into a ball and roll in chopped nuts. Serve with Ritz crackers.

recipes.title: Blueberry Cake
steps: Beat egg whites until stiff; add 1 cup sugar.
Set aside. Cream the shortening, salt, rest of sugar and vanilla.
Add egg yolks.
Beat until creamy.
Add baking powder, milk and flour to mixture alternately.
Fold in egg whites, then blueberries.
Pour into a well-greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sugar the top. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.

recipes.title: Never Fail Pie Crust(Double Pie Crust)
steps: Combine flour, sugar and salt.
Put shortening in a chilled bowl and add flour mixture.
Blend with pastry blender to a coarse meal.
Blend egg and ice cold water together, then add vinegar and blend.
Add to flour mixture and mix well.
Roll out on floured surface.

recipes.title: Best Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt the butter.
Pour into mixing bowl.
Beat in cocoa and sugar.
When mixture is smooth, beat in eggs, one at a time, then add vanilla.
Stir in flour, salt and coconut.
Pour in a 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Bake for 25 minutes. Let cool in pan and cut into squares.
Yields about 30 bars.

recipes.title: Toffee Brickle
steps: Line bottom of	lasagne
size
pan
with soda crackers. Boil sugar and
butter
about
8 minutes.
Pour over crackers. Bake at 350°
for 15 minutes.
Remove and sprinkle with chocolate chips. Spread melted chocolate chips with a knife.
Cool and crack into pieces.
